The vanadium electrolyte can be reused indefinitely and retains ~95% of its value at end-of-system-life — a different economics model than consumable lithium-ion cells.

Vanadium Pentoxide (V2O5).name: Vanadium Pentoxide (V2O5)
Vanadium Pentoxide (V2O5).descriptor_pill: Vanadium feedstock for both SCR catalysts and redox flow ...
Vanadium Pentoxide (V2O5).about: Vanadium feedstock for both SCR catalysts and redox flow electrolyte; dual-thesis node.
ai_summary: Vanadium oxide powder that serves as the feedstock for vanadium redox flow battery electrolyte and as a microalloying additive in high-strength steel.
Produced from vanadiferous titanomagnetite ores (China, Russia, South Africa) or as a byproduct of oil refining and uranium processing.
Global production is roughly 100,000 t/yr, with vanadium pentoxide prices historically volatile at $5–30/lb depending on steel demand cycles.
Each 4-hour, 10 MWh vanadium flow battery requires roughly 30–40 tonnes of V₂O₅ — large deployments need significant vanadium procurement.
V₂O₅ prices are currently driven by steel demand, but flow battery adoption at scale would create a new structural demand driver independent of the steel cycle.

Cadmium Telluride Film.name: Cadmium Telluride Film
Cadmium Telluride Film.descriptor_pill: Thin-film semiconductor deposited directly onto glass for...
Cadmium Telluride Film.about: Thin-film semiconductor deposited directly onto glass for First Solar PV modules.
ai_summary: Thin semiconductor layer deposited on glass to form the light-absorbing element of CdTe solar panels — First Solar's proprietary technology.
Made by co-depositing cadmium and tellurium in a vacuum chamber at temperatures around 500°C — First Solar is the only large-scale manufacturer.
Tellurium supply (~500–600 t/yr globally) is the binding constraint — it's a byproduct of copper refining and cannot scale independently.
CdTe panels are increasingly deployed for datacenter solar arrays in the US, where First Solar benefits from domestic manufacturing tax credits.
CdTe film is a vertically integrated product where one company (First Solar) controls the technology, manufacturing, and upstream tellurium sourcing.

Silver Conductive Paste.name: Silver Conductive Paste
Silver Conductive Paste.descriptor_pill: Front-contact metallization on c-Si solar cells; consumes...
Silver Conductive Paste.about: Front-contact metallization on c-Si solar cells; consumes ~10–15% of mined silver annually.
ai_summary: Silver powder suspended in glass frit and organic binders — screen-printed onto solar cells to form the electrical contacts that collect generated current.
Each GW of crystalline silicon solar capacity requires roughly 10–15 tonnes of silver — paste accounts for ~15% of global silver fabrication demand.
DuPont (now part of Heraeus), Heraeus, and Samsung SDI are leading paste producers — the silver intensity per cell is declining but not fast enough to offset volume growth.
Silver paste is consumed on every solar cell powering AI datacenters — the interface between photovoltaic physics and usable electricity.
Silver demand from solar is compounding on top of an already supply-constrained market — AI datacenter solar deployment adds another demand vector.

Solar Glass.name: Solar Glass
Solar Glass.descriptor_pill: Tempered low-iron glass front cover protecting PV cells f...
Solar Glass.about: Tempered low-iron glass front cover protecting PV cells from weather.
stats: Xinyi Solar, Flat Glass Group, Borosil
ai_summary: Low-iron tempered glass with anti-reflective coating — the front cover protecting solar cells from weather while maximizing light transmission.
Made from silica sand, soda ash, and limestone melted at ~1,500°C and rolled into sheets — low-iron formulations transmit ~91% of incident light versus ~83% for standard glass.
Xinyi Solar, Flat Glass Group, and other Chinese manufacturers dominate with ~80% of global solar glass capacity.
Each GW of solar PV capacity requires roughly 60,000–80,000 tonnes of solar glass — a bulk material consumed at enormous scale.
Solar glass is abundant and cheap but heavy — the logistics of shipping it from Chinese factories to global solar installation sites drive meaningful cost.

HALEU Fuel Assemblies.name: HALEU Fuel Assemblies
HALEU Fuel Assemblies.descriptor_pill: 5–20% enriched uranium fuel required by most SMR designs;...
HALEU Fuel Assemblies.about: 5–20% enriched uranium fuel required by most SMR designs; only Russia, China, and pilot-scale Centrus produce it.
ai_summary: Uranium fuel enriched to 5–20% U-235 and packaged into fuel rods — the higher enrichment lets reactor cores be smaller and run longer between refueling, which is why most small modular reactor designs need it.

Takes mined uranium and zirconium cladding tubes from upstream — the uranium is enriched in centrifuge cascades using export-controlled equipment, then loaded into zirconium alloy tubes that hold the fuel inside the reactor core.
Only Russia and China have commercial-scale HALEU enrichment today; the sole US source is a Centrus Energy demonstration plant in Ohio that has produced about 900 kg total through mid-2025.
The US banned Russian uranium imports in 2024 and committed $2.7 billion in January 2026 to build domestic capacity — but meaningful production is years away.
Every SMR being proposed for behind-the-meter AI datacenter power — by Microsoft, Google, Amazon — needs this fuel, and it essentially doesn't exist yet at Western commercial scale.

LEU Fuel Assemblies.name: LEU Fuel Assemblies
LEU Fuel Assemblies.descriptor_pill: Standard <5% enriched uranium fuel rods for conventional ...
LEU Fuel Assemblies.about: Standard <5% enriched uranium fuel rods for conventional light-water reactors.
ai_summary: Uranium fuel enriched to 3–5% U-235 — the standard fuel for existing light-water reactors that make up the global fleet of ~440 operating nuclear plants.
Enrichment is performed by Urenco (EU/UK), Orano (France), CNNC (China), and formerly Tenex (Russia, now restricted) using gas centrifuge cascades.
Existing nuclear plants are being extended and restarted specifically to power AI datacenters — Microsoft's Three Mile Island restart and Constellation's portfolio are leading examples.
LEU fuel supply chains are mature and diversified compared to HALEU — the constraint on conventional nuclear for datacenters is reactor permitting and grid access, not fuel.
LEU fuel is the near-term nuclear power pathway for AI datacenters — available today in operating reactors while HALEU-fueled SMRs remain years from deployment.

Zircaloy Cladding.name: Zircaloy Cladding
Zircaloy Cladding.descriptor_pill: Zirconium-alloy tubing encasing nuclear fuel pellets in b...
Zircaloy Cladding.about: Zirconium-alloy tubing encasing nuclear fuel pellets in both conventional reactors and SMRs.
ai_summary: Zirconium alloy tubing that encases nuclear fuel pellets inside reactor cores — the structural barrier between fuel and coolant, designed to withstand years of neutron bombardment.
Made from nuclear-grade zirconium that has been completely separated from hafnium (a neutron absorber) — only Westinghouse, Framatome, and TVEL perform this separation at scale.
Zircaloy must withstand temperatures above 1,200°C in accident scenarios while remaining transparent to neutrons during normal operation — a demanding materials specification.
Every nuclear fuel assembly — LEU or HALEU — requires zircaloy cladding tubes, making it a universal input to all nuclear power generation.
Zircaloy production is the bottleneck between zirconium supply and nuclear fuel fabrication — and the hafnium removed during purification feeds directly into chip manufacturing.

Tantalum Capacitors.name: Tantalum Capacitors
Tantalum Capacitors.descriptor_pill: High-reliability capacitors on every server board, switch...
Tantalum Capacitors.about: High-reliability capacitors on every server board, switch, and PSU.
ai_summary: Miniature capacitors using a tantalum metal anode, tantalum pentoxide dielectric, and manganese dioxide or conductive polymer cathode — valued for high capacitance density in small packages.
Tantalum powder is pressed and sintered into a porous pellet, anodized to grow a thin oxide dielectric, then encapsulated — a process requiring tightly controlled tantalum purity.
KEMET (now Yageo), AVX (now Kyocera AVX), and Vishay are the dominant manufacturers — ~50% of tantalum supply traces to artisanal DRC/Rwanda mining.
Every server board in an AI datacenter contains dozens of tantalum capacitors for power filtering and decoupling near processors and memory.
Tantalum capacitors link conflict-mineral supply chains directly to AI datacenter hardware — the DRC mine disruptions of 2024–2025 tightened supply of the components on every board.

Lead-Free Solder.name: Lead-Free Solder
Lead-Free Solder.descriptor_pill: SAC (tin-silver-copper) alloy bonding every component on ...
Lead-Free Solder.about: SAC (tin-silver-copper) alloy bonding every component on every board and package.
ai_summary: Tin-silver-copper alloy (typically SAC305) used to attach components to circuit boards — the material in every solder joint in every piece of electronic hardware.
Tin provides the base (~96.5%), silver adds strength (~3%), and copper prevents copper dissolution from the board pads (~0.5%) — mandated lead-free by RoHS since 2006.
Solder paste and preforms are supplied by Indium Corporation, Alpha (MacDermid), Senju, and others — a fragmented market with adequate supply.
Each AI server has thousands of solder joints; each GPU module has hundreds — a typical datacenter rack contains millions of individual connections.
Solder is consumed in vast quantities but rarely constrained — the upstream tin supply is the more relevant bottleneck.

Gold Bond Wire.name: Gold Bond Wire
Gold Bond Wire.descriptor_pill: Ultra-fine gold wire bonding chip die to package leadfram...
Gold Bond Wire.about: Ultra-fine gold wire bonding chip die to package leadframes and ENIG PCB finishes.
ai_summary: Ultra-thin gold wire (15–50 µm diameter) used to connect chip die pads to package leads — the traditional interconnect method for wire-bonded semiconductors.
Drawn from 4N+ gold (99.99% pure) into spools of wire that automated bonders loop between chip and leadframe at rates of 10–15 bonds per second.
Copper bond wire has replaced gold in most cost-sensitive packages, but gold remains standard for automotive, military, and high-reliability applications.
In AI datacenters, gold wire appears primarily in power management ICs, sensors, and discrete components rather than in the GPUs themselves.
Gold wire is a legacy interconnect being displaced by copper — still present but shrinking in share across the semiconductor industry.

YSZ Electrolyte.name: YSZ Electrolyte
YSZ Electrolyte.descriptor_pill: Yttria-stabilized zirconia ceramic electrolyte at the hea...
YSZ Electrolyte.about: Yttria-stabilized zirconia ceramic electrolyte at the heart of solid-oxide fuel cells.
ai_summary: Yttria-stabilized zirconia ceramic — the solid electrolyte membrane at the heart of solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) that converts fuel to electricity at ~60% efficiency.
Made by mixing zirconium oxide with ~8% yttrium oxide, pressing into thin sheets, and sintering at 1,400°C+ to form a dense, ion-conducting ceramic.
Bloom Energy is the leading commercial SOFC manufacturer deploying these electrolyte stacks for onsite datacenter power generation.
YSZ electrolyte enables fuel cells that can run on natural gas, hydrogen, or biogas — flexible fuel inputs for sites where grid power isn't available fast enough.
If SOFCs scale as behind-the-meter datacenter power, YSZ ceramics shift from a niche material to a structural input in the AI power chain.

Engineered Coolants.name: Engineered Coolants
Engineered Coolants.descriptor_pill: EGW blends for direct-to-chip and fluorinated dielectric ...
Engineered Coolants.about: EGW blends for direct-to-chip and fluorinated dielectric fluids for immersion cooling.
ai_summary: Specialized dielectric fluids (fluorinated or hydrocarbon-based) circulated through direct-to-chip and immersion cooling systems to remove heat from AI processors.
3M Novec (discontinued 2025), Solvay Galden, and engineered mineral oils are the primary fluid chemistries — each with different thermal, safety, and environmental profiles.
3M's exit from PFAS-based fluids (Novec) removed the most widely deployed immersion coolant from the market, forcing rapid qualification of alternatives.
Liquid cooling is becoming mandatory for AI GPU racks running at 40–120 kW — air cooling alone cannot dissipate the heat density of Blackwell-class systems.
The engineered coolant market is in rapid transition as PFAS regulation eliminates established products while AI heat loads demand more liquid cooling, not less.

Refrigerants.name: Refrigerants
Refrigerants.descriptor_pill: HFC, HFO, or ammonia working fluids in chiller vapor-comp...
Refrigerants.about: HFC, HFO, or ammonia working fluids in chiller vapor-compression cycles.
ai_summary: Chemical compounds cycled through compression-expansion loops to move heat from datacenter interiors to outdoor rejection — the working fluid in every chiller and CRAC unit.
Traditional HFCs (R-134a, R-410A) are being phased down under the Kigali Amendment; lower-GWP HFOs (R-1234yf, R-1234ze) and natural refrigerants (CO₂, propane) are replacing them.
Chemours, Honeywell, and Daikin are leading refrigerant producers — the HFC-to-HFO transition has created temporary supply tightness in some formulations.
Every datacenter chiller plant, precision cooling unit, and heat pump operates on a refrigerant charge — the choice of refrigerant affects efficiency, cost, and regulatory compliance.
The refrigerant transition is adding cost and complexity to datacenter cooling just as AI heat loads are scaling — a convergence of regulatory pressure and physical demand.

Clean Fire-Suppression Agents.name: Clean Fire-Suppression Agents
Clean Fire-Suppression Agents.descriptor_pill: FM-200 and Novec 1230 fluorinated agents for fire suppres...
Clean Fire-Suppression Agents.about: FM-200 and Novec 1230 fluorinated agents for fire suppression in IT spaces.
ai_summary: Gaseous agents (FM-200, Novec 1230, inert gas blends) deployed in datacenter white space to extinguish fires without damaging electronic equipment or leaving residue.
Novec 1230 (3M) was the preferred agent but is being phased out with 3M's PFAS exit — FK-5-1-12 alternatives and inert gas systems (IG-541, Argonite) are replacing it.
Every datacenter white space, electrical room, and generator enclosure requires a clean fire-suppression system — Tier III and IV standards mandate automatic suppression.
The transition away from PFAS-based suppressants is creating qualification delays and cost increases for new datacenter builds.
Clean suppression agents are a regulatory-driven supply chain transition happening in parallel with the datacenter buildout — the old standard product is disappearing.

Transformer Oil.name: Transformer Oil
Transformer Oil.descriptor_pill: Mineral, synthetic ester, or silicone fluid insulating an...
Transformer Oil.about: Mineral, synthetic ester, or silicone fluid insulating and cooling transformer cores.
ai_summary: Mineral oil or synthetic ester fluid that insulates and cools power transformers — filling the tank of every step-down and distribution transformer in a datacenter power chain.
Mineral oil (naphthenic-based) is the traditional choice; synthetic esters (Midel, Envirotemp) are gaining share for fire safety and environmental advantages.
Nynas, Ergon, and Cargill (Envirotemp) are major suppliers — transformer oil is a commodity but availability can tighten when transformer deliveries surge.
Every transformer between the utility feed and the server rack contains hundreds to thousands of gallons of insulating oil.
Transformer oil is a bulk consumable that scales with the transformer delivery pipeline — currently tracking the same 2–3 year lead-time bottleneck as the transformers themselves.

XLPE Insulation Compound.name: XLPE Insulation Compound
XLPE Insulation Compound.descriptor_pill: Cross-linked polyethylene insulation around HV/MV power c...
XLPE Insulation Compound.about: Cross-linked polyethylene insulation around HV/MV power cable conductors.
ai_summary: Cross-linked polyethylene — the polymer extruded around copper or aluminum conductors to form the insulating jacket on medium-voltage and high-voltage power cables.
Produced by cross-linking polyethylene pellets using peroxide catalysts during the cable extrusion process — the cross-linking makes it thermally stable up to 90°C continuous operation.
Borealis, Dow, and Chinese compound makers supply the base resin; cable manufacturers (Nexans, Prysmian, Southwire) perform the extrusion and cross-linking.
Every medium-voltage feeder and high-voltage transmission cable connecting a datacenter to the grid uses XLPE insulation.
XLPE compound supply is generally adequate — the constraint in datacenter power cabling is more often cable manufacturing capacity and installation labor than raw insulation material.

SF6 / C4-FN Insulating Gas.name: SF6 / C4-FN Insulating Gas
SF6 / C4-FN Insulating Gas.descriptor_pill: Dielectric gas in MV/HV switchgear; SF6 being phased to l...
SF6 / C4-FN Insulating Gas.about: Dielectric gas in MV/HV switchgear; SF6 being phased to lower-GWP C4-FN/CO2 mixes.
ai_summary: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF₆) is the traditional insulating gas in high-voltage switchgear — the most potent greenhouse gas regulated under the Kyoto Protocol (23,500x CO₂ GWP).
C4-FN (3M Novec 4710, now Hitachi's alternative blends) offers ~99% lower GWP while maintaining similar dielectric performance — the leading SF₆ replacement.
Every HV switchgear assembly at a datacenter substation contains insulating gas — either SF₆ in legacy equipment or C4-FN in new installations.
EU F-gas regulation is phasing down SF₆ in new equipment; US utilities and hyperscalers are voluntarily transitioning to reduce Scope 3 emissions.
The SF₆-to-C4-FN transition adds cost to datacenter HV infrastructure but is increasingly mandated — another PFAS-adjacent supply chain reshuffling.

Underfill Resin.name: Underfill Resin
Underfill Resin.descriptor_pill: Capillary-flow epoxy filling gaps between chip die and su...
Underfill Resin.about: Capillary-flow epoxy filling gaps between chip die and substrate to absorb thermal stress.
ai_summary: Epoxy-based liquid dispensed between a flip-chip die and its substrate, then cured to a solid — it mechanically locks the chip in place and protects the solder bumps from thermal stress.
Applied after the chip is mounted and reflowed — flows by capillary action into the gap between die and substrate, filling every void.
Namics, Henkel, and Hitachi Chemical are leading suppliers — the material must match the thermal expansion coefficients of silicon and substrate to prevent cracking.
Every flip-chip package in an AI datacenter — GPUs, CPUs, ASICs — uses underfill to survive the thermal cycling of power-on/power-off loads.
Underfill is a small-volume specialty chemical that's invisible inside the package but essential to long-term chip reliability.

Epoxy Resin.name: Epoxy Resin
Epoxy Resin.descriptor_pill: Polymer matrix for ABF substrate, FR-4 laminate, and unde...
Epoxy Resin.about: Polymer matrix for ABF substrate, FR-4 laminate, and underfill compounds.
ai_summary: Thermoset polymer made from epichlorohydrin and bisphenol A — the binder that holds fiberglass together in PCB laminates and provides structural rigidity.
Cured by mixing with a hardener (amine or anhydride) and heating — once set, epoxy cannot be remelted, giving PCBs their permanent shape.
Dow, Huntsman, and Hexion are major epoxy producers — supply is commodity-scale and generally adequate.
Every printed circuit board in a datacenter is built on an epoxy-fiberglass composite — the material that gives boards their characteristic green color and structural stiffness.
Epoxy resin is a bulk petrochemical derivative consumed in vast quantities across electronics manufacturing — structurally ubiquitous but not supply-constrained.

Fiberglass.name: Fiberglass
Fiberglass.descriptor_pill: Glass reinforcement in PCB laminate, wind turbine blades,...
Fiberglass.about: Glass reinforcement in PCB laminate, wind turbine blades, and cooling tower fill.
ai_summary: Woven fabric of spun glass filaments — the reinforcement material laminated with epoxy resin to form the structural core of all FR-4 printed circuit boards.
Made by melting silica sand and extruding it through bushings into ultra-thin filaments, then weaving them into standardized cloth grades (E-glass, T-glass).
High-end T-glass (thin-thread glass) required for high-speed AI server boards is in tight supply — standard E-glass is abundant.
Every server board, switch card, and power supply PCB in a datacenter contains multiple layers of fiberglass-reinforced laminate.
T-glass supply is a quiet constraint on high-speed PCB production — the gap between commodity fiberglass and server-grade glass cloth is where the shortage sits.

Trichlorosilane (TCS).name: Trichlorosilane (TCS)
Trichlorosilane (TCS).descriptor_pill: Gaseous silicon precursor in the Siemens process producin...
Trichlorosilane (TCS).about: Gaseous silicon precursor in the Siemens process producing polysilicon.
ai_summary: Chlorosilane gas (HSiCl₃) produced by reacting metallurgical silicon with hydrochloric acid — the intermediate chemical that carries silicon through purification to polysilicon.
Distilled repeatedly to remove impurities down to parts-per-trillion levels before being decomposed back into solid polysilicon in Siemens reactors.
The same molecule serves both solar and electronic polysilicon production — the purity of distillation determines which grade comes out.
Major producers include Wacker, Hemlock, OCI, and Chinese chemical plants — production capacity tracks polysilicon demand.
TCS is the chemical workhorse of silicon purification — invisible to end users but consumed in enormous volumes to feed both the chip and solar supply chains.

Ultra-Pure Water.name: Ultra-Pure Water
Ultra-Pure Water.descriptor_pill: 18 MΩ·cm DI water used by the millions of gallons in wafe...
Ultra-Pure Water.about: 18 MΩ·cm DI water used by the millions of gallons in wafer fabs; siting constraint for new fabs.
ai_summary: Water purified to 18.2 MΩ·cm resistivity (essentially zero dissolved ions) — consumed in vast quantities at every semiconductor fab for rinsing wafers between process steps.
Produced from municipal water through reverse osmosis, deionization, UV treatment, and ultrafiltration — a multi-stage purification train running continuously.
Each 300mm wafer requires roughly 2,000–5,000 gallons of UPW; a large fab consumes millions of gallons per day.
Veolia, Evoqua (now Xylem), and Ovivo supply the purification systems — the water itself comes from local sources, making fab siting depend on water availability.
UPW is the most voluminous consumable in chip manufacturing — abundant as a feedstock but requiring enormous infrastructure to purify to semiconductor grade.

Semiconductor Specialty Solvents.name: Semiconductor Specialty Solvents
Semiconductor Specialty Solvents.descriptor_pill: PGMEA, IPA, NMP and other ultra-pure solvents in photores...
Semiconductor Specialty Solvents.about: PGMEA, IPA, NMP and other ultra-pure solvents in photoresist, etch, and clean chemistries.
ai_summary: High-purity organic solvents (PGMEA, NMP, IPA, acetone) used to develop photoresist, clean wafers, and strip coatings during chip fabrication.
Purity requirements are extreme — parts-per-trillion metallic contamination levels, requiring dedicated distillation facilities separate from industrial chemical production.
Major suppliers include Honeywell, BASF, and KMG Chemicals (now CMC Materials) — a specialized segment of the broader chemical industry.
Consumed at every fab in every process step that involves photoresist application, development, or removal — volumes scale with wafer starts.
Specialty solvents are a quiet consumable in chip manufacturing — unglamorous but structurally essential to yield at every process node.

Cerium Oxide.name: Cerium Oxide
Cerium Oxide.descriptor_pill: Light rare earth abrasive for CMP slurries polishing wafe...
Cerium Oxide.about: Light rare earth abrasive for CMP slurries polishing wafers between fab layers.
ai_summary: Fine powder of cerium dioxide (CeO₂) used as the primary abrasive in CMP slurries for polishing semiconductor wafer surfaces — the most common rare earth compound in chip manufacturing.
Produced by calcining cerium carbonate or cerium hydroxide precipitated from rare earth separation — China refines ~85% of global cerium output.
Particle size distribution must be tightly controlled — oversized particles scratch the wafer, undersized particles don't polish, and either outcome kills yield.
Every advanced chip goes through multiple CMP steps using cerium-based slurries — demand scales with wafer complexity and AI chip production volumes.
Cerium oxide is cheap (~$2/kg) and abundant by rare earth standards, but its semiconductor-grade form requires purity that only a few processors can consistently deliver.

Germanium.name: Germanium
Germanium.descriptor_pill: Trace metal feedstock for GeCl4 (fiber optics, IR optics,...
Germanium.about: Trace metal feedstock for GeCl4 (fiber optics, IR optics, SiGe transistors, PET catalysts).
ai_summary: Silvery metalloid used to dope the glass that carries light through fiber optic cables.
Recovered as a byproduct of zinc smelting and coal fly ash — never mined directly.
China produces ~60% of global supply; Western-accessible volume is ~80 t/yr against ~220 t/yr global.
Banned to the US in late 2024, ban suspended in November 2025, but US imports from China have been zero since 2023.
Prices have roughly doubled since 2022 with no Western substitute at scale.
AI datacenter fiber demand is scaling exponentially — germanium is the cleanest chokepoint setup in the chain.

Gallium.name: Gallium
Gallium.descriptor_pill: Substrate metal for GaN power transistors and GaAs lasers...
Gallium.about: Substrate metal for GaN power transistors and GaAs lasers; ~98% Chinese primary supply.
ai_summary: Soft metal whose value comes from forming the compound semiconductors in laser chips (GaAs) and power chips (GaN).
Almost exclusively a byproduct of bauxite refining for aluminum — China produces ~98% of primary supply globally.
Under Chinese export licensing since 2023, full US export ban from late 2024 to late 2025.
China also restricted the separation technology that would let Western producers scale.
~600 t/yr of refined production supports hundreds of billions in downstream markets.
GaN power chips and GaAs lasers are growing fast in AI infrastructure just as China tightens the entire chain.

Indium.name: Indium
Indium.descriptor_pill: Metal feedstock for InP wafers underlying every high-spee...
Indium.about: Metal feedstock for InP wafers underlying every high-speed transceiver laser and photodiode.
ai_summary: Soft metal that pairs with phosphorus to form the substrate underlying nearly every high-speed laser in optical communications.
Recovered as a byproduct of zinc refining, with China leading global supply.
Only ~900 tonnes produced globally per year — a small market enabling tens of billions in downstream products.
Added to China's late-2025 export control list before the broader suspension.
Each transceiver generation (400G → 800G → 1.6T) uses more indium per device.
Co-packaged optics, the next-gen architecture, uses even more InP — and there's no large fungible capacity to flex.

Tantalum.name: Tantalum
Tantalum.descriptor_pill: Feedstock for tantalum capacitors and turbine superalloy ...
Tantalum.about: Feedstock for tantalum capacitors and turbine superalloy alloying.
ai_summary: Dense, corrosion-resistant metal used in highly reliable capacitors and in superalloys for turbine blades.
~50% of supply comes from artisanal mining in DRC and Rwanda; most Western volume is a byproduct of Australian lithium mines.
April 2024 M23 capture of the Rubaya mine and May 2025 mine collapse have tightened African supply.
~1,700 t/yr concentrate production, with Chinese imports of Rwandan material up 82% since 2023.
Every AI server board has many tantalum capacitors — they're irreplaceable for high-density, high-reliability energy storage.
AI datacenter demand has become a major incremental driver just as the DRC supply situation deteriorates.

Tungsten.name: Tungsten
Tungsten.descriptor_pill: Chip BEOL interconnect plugs, superalloy alloying, SCR ca...
Tungsten.about: Chip BEOL interconnect plugs, superalloy alloying, SCR catalyst support.
ai_summary: The metal with the highest melting point of any element — used in chip interconnects, cutting tools, and turbine alloys.
China produces ~83% of mined tungsten and controls ~75% of refining capacity.
Sits inside every advanced logic chip as the plug metal in BEOL interconnects.
Also alloyed into nickel superalloys for gas turbine blades.
China cut its 2025 mining quota and added tungsten to its export control list — refined prices hit a 12-year high mid-2025.
Tungsten sits inside both the most strategic AI chips and the most constrained datacenter power infrastructure.

Cobalt.name: Cobalt
Cobalt.descriptor_pill: Superalloy alloying element for turbine blades; ~70% DRC ...
Cobalt.about: Superalloy alloying element for turbine blades; ~70% DRC mining, ~75% China refining.
ai_summary: Transition metal used in lithium-ion battery cathodes (NMC chemistry), superalloys for gas turbines, and cemented carbides for cutting tools.
~70% of global mine production comes from the DRC, with most refined output processed in China.
Global production is roughly 190,000 t/yr, with artisanal mining in the DRC raising persistent ethical sourcing concerns.
In AI datacenters, cobalt appears in NMC battery backup systems, turbine superalloys for onsite gas power, and cutting tools for construction.
LFP batteries (cobalt-free) are displacing NMC for stationary storage, which may reduce datacenter cobalt exposure over time.
Cobalt's AI infrastructure role is shrinking as LFP gains share in BESS, but it remains embedded in turbine alloys and legacy backup systems.

Rhenium.name: Rhenium
Rhenium.descriptor_pill: Single-crystal superalloy input for high-temp turbine bla...
Rhenium.about: Single-crystal superalloy input for high-temp turbine blades; ~50 t/yr global supply.
ai_summary: One of the rarest elements in Earth's crust, with an extremely high melting point and no substitute in single-crystal turbine alloys.
Almost entirely a byproduct of molybdenum production — Chile produces ~50% of global supply.
Only ~50 tonnes produced globally per year, worth roughly $200M annually.
Key alloying element for the highest-temperature blades in the gas turbines being deployed for onsite datacenter power.
Cannot scale independently — supply is gated three layers down the byproduct chain behind copper.
Every gigawatt of onsite gas power for AI datacenters is bottlenecked by this metal.

Hafnium.name: Hafnium
Hafnium.descriptor_pill: High-k gate dielectric in advanced-node logic; nickel-sup...
Hafnium.about: High-k gate dielectric in advanced-node logic; nickel-superalloy and zircaloy stabilizer.
ai_summary: Transition metal whose strategic value comes from being the high-k gate dielectric inside every advanced logic chip.
Produced almost entirely as a byproduct of nuclear-grade zirconium separation.
~70-80 t/yr of refined production globally at prices in the $1,000+/kg range.
Supply is mechanically linked to nuclear-grade zirconium demand from reactor builds.
Advanced AI chips need more hafnium per wafer as nodes shrink below 5nm.
The unusual structure means SMR deployment for AI power may actually loosen hafnium supply as the upstream zirconium chain scales.

Molybdenum.name: Molybdenum
Molybdenum.descriptor_pill: Alloying element in stainless steels and superalloys; rhe...
Molybdenum.about: Alloying element in stainless steels and superalloys; rhenium is largely a moly byproduct.
ai_summary: High-melting-point metal used as an alloying element in stainless steel, structural steels, and superalloys.
Produced both as a primary metal and as a byproduct of copper mining — Chile, China, the US, and Peru lead global supply.
~250,000 t/yr of mine production — large by specialty-metal standards.
Makes 316-grade stainless steel resistant to corrosion in datacenter cooling systems.
Also alloyed into turbine superalloys and the structural steels used in datacenter construction.
Less acute than other specialty metals, but molybdenum is the upstream source of rhenium and tracks copper market dynamics.

Chromium.name: Chromium
Chromium.descriptor_pill: Stainless steel and superalloy alloying element; ferrochr...
Chromium.about: Stainless steel and superalloy alloying element; ferrochrome feedstock.
ai_summary: Metal whose primary value is corrosion resistance — the defining element in stainless steel (minimum 10.5% Cr content by definition).
Global ferrochrome production is roughly 17 million t/yr, with South Africa (~45%) and Kazakhstan as leading producers.
316-grade stainless steel, which requires 16–18% chromium, is the standard material for datacenter cooling piping, heat exchangers, and manifolds.
Also alloyed into nickel-based superalloys for gas turbine hot-section components used in datacenter power generation.
Supply is geographically concentrated but generally adequate — South African ferrochrome output is periodically constrained by electricity load-shedding.
Chromium is a structural enabler of datacenter thermal and power infrastructure — constrained not by geology but by South African grid reliability.

Nickel.name: Nickel
Nickel.descriptor_pill: Stainless steel base, superalloy base metal, and fuel cel...
Nickel.about: Stainless steel base, superalloy base metal, and fuel cell electrode current collectors.
ai_summary: Versatile metal used in stainless steel, battery cathodes (NMC), and the nickel-based superalloys that withstand turbine operating temperatures.
Global mine production is roughly 3.3 million t/yr, with Indonesia (~50%), Philippines, Russia, and New Caledonia as top producers.
Indonesia's massive laterite nickel expansion has shifted global supply, with Chinese-financed HPAL and RKEF plants dominating new capacity.
In AI datacenters, nickel appears in stainless steel cooling systems, NMC battery backup, and the Inconel/Waspaloy superalloys inside gas turbines.
Class 1 nickel (battery and alloy grade) trades at a premium to ferronickel (stainless grade) — the two markets have partially decoupled.
Nickel is embedded across power, thermal, and structural layers of the datacenter — not a single chokepoint but a pervasive dependency.

Neodymium.name: Neodymium
Neodymium.descriptor_pill: Primary rare-earth element in NdFeB permanent magnets.
Neodymium.about: Primary rare-earth element in NdFeB permanent magnets.
ai_summary: Silver-gray rare earth that, alloyed with iron and boron, forms the strongest permanent magnets commercially available.
China controls ~85% of global NdFeB magnet production and refines roughly 60% of the world's neodymium oxide.
Global NdFeB magnet output was around 220,000 tonnes in 2024, with demand forecast to grow ~8% annually driven by EVs and AI infrastructure.
China imposed export controls on rare earth processing technology in late 2023, then tightened further in 2025 with licensing requirements on magnet-grade exports.
Every HDD spindle motor and datacenter cooling fan contains an NdFeB magnet — each GPU server rack requires dozens across storage and thermal management.
AI datacenter build-out and EV demand are compounding on the same magnet supply — neodymium sits at the intersection of the decade's two largest hardware scaling curves.

Praseodymium.name: Praseodymium
Praseodymium.descriptor_pill: Light rare earth co-substituted with neodymium in NdFeB m...
Praseodymium.about: Light rare earth co-substituted with neodymium in NdFeB magnets; usually sold as didymium.
ai_summary: Light rare earth almost always sold as didymium (NdPr oxide, ~75% Nd / 25% Pr), because the two elements are commercially inseparable without prohibitive cost.
China controls ~85–90% of global NdPr oxide output; prices traded in the $50–70/kg range through 2024–2025 after collapsing from a 2022 peak near $130/kg.
Substitutes for neodymium atom-for-atom in NdFeB sintered magnets powering EV motors, industrial robots, and datacenter cooling and storage systems.
MP Materials (Mountain Pass, California) and Lynas Rare Earths (Mount Weld, Australia) are the only large-scale non-Chinese NdPr producers.
China extended licensing requirements on magnet-grade NdPr exports in mid-2025, pressuring non-Chinese magnet supply chains serving defense and EV sectors.
NdPr has no drop-in substitute in high-performance permanent magnets — as AI and defense programs both demand domestically sourced magnets, supply outside China becomes a structural chokepoint.

Dysprosium.name: Dysprosium
Dysprosium.descriptor_pill: Heavy rare earth stabilizing NdFeB magnets at high operat...
Dysprosium.about: Heavy rare earth stabilizing NdFeB magnets at high operating temperatures.
stats: Shenghe, China Northern Rare Earth, Lynas
ai_summary: Heavy rare earth added at 1–6% by weight to NdFeB magnets to prevent demagnetization above 80°C — structurally irreplaceable in high-performance motors.
Global production runs roughly 1,500–2,000 t/yr, with China controlling ~90% of output from ionic adsorption clay deposits in southern provinces and Myanmar.
Unlike light rare earths from hard-rock mines, dysprosium occurs only in trace concentrations in ionic clay ores — supply is structurally inelastic.
Myanmar, which supplied 50–70% of the ionic clay ore feeding Chinese separation plants, saw armed-conflict-driven border closures in 2024–2025 that spiked prices above $250/kg.
In AI infrastructure, dysprosium-bearing magnets sit in HDD motors, cooling fans, and the wind turbines increasingly used to power or offset datacenter loads.
China's 2023–2025 export controls on separation technology close off the fastest route to non-Chinese refining — any magnet-dependent AI supply chain carries a concentrated single point of failure.

Terbium.name: Terbium
Terbium.descriptor_pill: Heavy rare earth boosting magnetic performance in high-te...
Terbium.about: Heavy rare earth boosting magnetic performance in high-temp NdFeB grades.
stats: Shenghe, China Northern Rare Earth, Northern Minerals
ai_summary: Heavy rare earth added in small quantities (0.1–0.3 wt%) to NdFeB magnets to raise coercivity, allowing full performance above 150°C.
Global production is roughly 300–400 t/yr — one of the scarcest commercially traded rare earths by absolute volume.
China controls ~85–90% of supply, sourced from the same ionic clay deposits in Jiangxi and Fujian that produce dysprosium.
Co-extracted with dysprosium from identical ore bodies — any supply disruption to one element simultaneously constrains the other.
Spot prices have historically ranged $700–2,000/kg, spiking during China's 2010–2011 export quota crisis and again during 2022–2023 trade restriction signaling.
Terbium sits at the narrowest bottleneck in the magnet supply chain — low volume, zero Western primary production, and no substitute.

Cerium.name: Cerium
Cerium.descriptor_pill: Most abundant rare earth; feeds CMP slurries, glass polis...
Cerium.about: Most abundant rare earth; feeds CMP slurries, glass polishing, and catalysts.
ai_summary: Most abundant rare earth element, extracted as a co-product of bastnäsite and monazite ore processing in China, Australia, and the US.
Global cerium oxide production runs 40,000–60,000 t/yr, with China accounting for ~85–90% of refined output.
Cerium oxide is the dominant abrasive in CMP slurries — the polishing process repeated dozens of times per wafer at every advanced semiconductor fab.
CMP demand tied to AI chips is rising because HBM stacking and dense interconnect layers require more polishing steps per wafer.
Cerium carbonate spot prices remain in the $1–2/kg range, far below dysprosium (~$300/kg) or terbium (~$700/kg), reflecting abundance.
Despite low unit prices, cerium is a consumable at every advanced fab — any export restriction or purity disruption would propagate directly into wafer yield.

Yttrium.name: Yttrium
Yttrium.descriptor_pill: Stabilizer in YSZ ceramic electrolyte at the heart of sol...
Yttrium.about: Stabilizer in YSZ ceramic electrolyte at the heart of solid-oxide fuel cells.
ai_summary: Rare earth element whose primary AI-infrastructure role is stabilizing the YSZ ceramic electrolyte inside solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs).
China produces roughly 60–70% of global yttrium oxide, with total production around 8,000–10,000 t/yr.
Also used in LED phosphors, laser crystals, and high-temperature ceramics, but the SOFC application carries the AI thesis.
Bloom Energy deploys solid oxide fuel cells for onsite datacenter power — each system uses yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte stacks.
Yttrium prices sit in the $3–5/kg oxide range, low by rare earth standards but structurally tied to Chinese supply decisions.
If SOFCs scale as an onsite power solution for AI datacenters that can't wait for grid upgrades, yttrium demand inflects from a niche into a structural input.

Helium.name: Helium
Helium.descriptor_pill: Cryogenic cooling and inert atmosphere for fabs; sealing ...
Helium.about: Cryogenic cooling and inert atmosphere for fabs; sealing gas for high-capacity HDDs.
ai_summary: Noble gas with the lowest boiling point of any element — used for cryogenic cooling, fiber draw tower purge, and leak detection in semiconductor fabs.
Global production is roughly 160 million cubic meters per year, with the US (~30%), Qatar (~30%), and Algeria (~10%) as top sources.
Helium cannot be synthesized — it is extracted from natural gas fields where it accumulated over billions of years of radioactive decay.
The US Federal Helium Reserve in Amarillo, Texas was fully privatized in 2023, removing the strategic buffer that had stabilized supply for decades.
Fiber optic cable drawing consumes helium as the cooling gas — every strand-km of fiber requires ~0.5 liters, with no substitute.
Three independent AI infrastructure inputs — fiber drawing, chip fab cooling, and HDD manufacturing — all compete for the same non-renewable helium supply.

Neon.name: Neon
Neon.descriptor_pill: ArF excimer laser gas (>96% of mix) for DUV lithography o...
Neon.about: ArF excimer laser gas (>96% of mix) for DUV lithography on every advanced chip.
ai_summary: Noble gas used as the primary medium in excimer lasers that pattern the most advanced semiconductor chips.
Prior to 2022, Ukraine supplied roughly 50% of global semiconductor-grade neon, purified from air-separation byproducts of steel mills in Odesa and Mariupol.
Russia's invasion of Ukraine disrupted neon supply, triggering emergency diversification to US, Chinese, and South Korean purification capacity.
DUV lithography — the workhorse patterning technology for mature-node chips powering power supplies, controllers, and sensors in AI datacenters — consumes neon in every exposure.
Prices spiked 10–20x during the initial 2022 disruption before partially normalizing as new capacity came online.
The Ukraine-sourced supply chain has permanently restructured, but the gas remains a single-point sensitivity for any fab running DUV steppers.

Krypton.name: Krypton
Krypton.descriptor_pill: KrF lasers and high-aspect-ratio etch gas for 3D NAND sca...
Krypton.about: KrF lasers and high-aspect-ratio etch gas for 3D NAND scaling beyond 300 layers.
ai_summary: Noble gas used in semiconductor fabs for ion implantation and as an etch gas in advanced memory manufacturing.
Co-produced with neon during cryogenic air separation — supply tracks steel industry oxygen demand rather than semiconductor demand.
Global production is modest at roughly 40–50 tonnes per year, with Russia and Ukraine historically supplying a significant share.
Used in DRAM and NAND flash manufacturing processes that produce the memory chips stacked in HBM modules for AI accelerators.
Prices surged alongside neon during the 2022 Ukraine supply shock and have partially normalized as alternative purification sources scaled.
Krypton's co-production economics mean it cannot scale independently — supply is gated by air separation volumes driven by the steel industry.

Xenon.name: Xenon
Xenon.descriptor_pill: EUV lithography light source plasma generating 13.5 nm ra...
Xenon.about: EUV lithography light source plasma generating 13.5 nm radiation for sub-7 nm nodes.
ai_summary: Heaviest stable noble gas, used in semiconductor fabs for ion implantation, plasma etching, and satellite electric propulsion.
Global production is roughly 40–50 tonnes per year — one of the scarcest industrial gases by volume.
Co-produced with krypton during air separation, making it structurally supply-linked to steel production and neon purification capacity.
In chip manufacturing, xenon is used in selective etching steps for advanced logic and 3D NAND — processes central to AI chip and storage production.
Prices remain elevated relative to pre-2022 levels following the Ukraine-driven noble gas supply restructuring.
Xenon's extreme scarcity and co-production constraints make it a quiet but real bottleneck for any sustained expansion of advanced chip and memory fab capacity.

Argon.name: Argon
Argon.descriptor_pill: Bulk inert gas for sputtering, annealing, and ingot growt...
Argon.about: Bulk inert gas for sputtering, annealing, and ingot growth across all wafer fabs.
ai_summary: Noble gas produced in large volumes as a byproduct of cryogenic air separation — the same plants that produce industrial oxygen and nitrogen.
Global production is roughly 700,000 tonnes per year, making it orders of magnitude more abundant than neon, krypton, or xenon.
Used as an inert shielding gas in semiconductor fabs during sputtering, CVD, and crystal growth processes.
Also consumed in steelmaking (argon-oxygen decarburization) and welding — both relevant to datacenter structural construction.
Supply is generally adequate and tracks industrial gas demand, with Air Liquide, Linde, and Air Products as dominant producers.
Argon is the least constrained noble gas in the AI supply chain — a commodity input rather than a chokepoint.

Ammonia.name: Ammonia
Ammonia.descriptor_pill: Nitrogen source for GaN epitaxy and a feedstock for chip-...
Ammonia.about: Nitrogen source for GaN epitaxy and a feedstock for chip-fab process chemistries.
ai_summary: Synthesized from nitrogen and hydrogen via the Haber-Bosch process — one of the most energy-intensive industrial chemical processes.
Global production exceeds 180 million t/yr, primarily for fertilizer, but increasingly explored as a hydrogen carrier and clean fuel.
In AI infrastructure, ammonia-based cooling systems are used in large-scale datacenter heat rejection and industrial chillers.
Green ammonia (produced from renewable hydrogen) is being developed as a zero-carbon fuel for backup generators and fuel cells.
Production is geographically distributed — China, Russia, India, and the US are the largest producers.
Ammonia's AI-infrastructure role is secondary but growing as datacenter operators explore alternatives to diesel backup and natural gas cooling.

Chlorine.name: Chlorine
Chlorine.descriptor_pill: Reactive halogen used to chlorinate germanium and silicon...
Chlorine.about: Reactive halogen used to chlorinate germanium and silicon precursors (GeCl4, TCS).
ai_summary: Produced by electrolysis of brine (salt water), always co-produced with sodium hydroxide (caustic soda) in a fixed ratio.
Global production exceeds 75 million t/yr, with the chlor-alkali industry concentrated in China, the US, and Europe.
In AI infrastructure, chlorine is the feedstock for germanium tetrachloride (GeCl₄), the compound that dopes fiber optic cable cores.
Also feeds into PVC production for cable insulation and jacketing used throughout datacenter wiring.
Supply is generally adequate but tracks caustic soda demand — chlorine is sometimes the unwanted co-product, creating price volatility.
Chlorine sits upstream of the fiber optic chokepoint — every kilometer of fiber cable traces back to chlorine chemistry.

Fluorspar.name: Fluorspar
Fluorspar.descriptor_pill: Calcium fluoride ore feeding HF and all downstream fluoro...
Fluorspar.about: Calcium fluoride ore feeding HF and all downstream fluorochemicals; ~65% China supply.
ai_summary: Calcium fluoride mineral mined primarily in China (~60%), Mexico, and South Africa — the primary source of fluorine for industrial chemistry.
Global mine production is roughly 8 million t/yr, feeding hydrofluoric acid production for refrigerants, fluoropolymers, and semiconductor etchants.
Fluorine-derived etchants (NF₃, SF₆, CF₄) are consumed in every semiconductor fab for chamber cleaning and plasma etching.
China classified fluorspar as a strategic mineral and has periodically restricted exports, creating price spikes in downstream fluorochemicals.
Acid-grade fluorspar (>97% CaF₂) commands a premium and is the bottleneck grade for semiconductor and refrigerant applications.
Fluorspar is three steps upstream of the chip fab — but every advanced logic and memory wafer requires fluorine chemistry that traces back to this mineral.

Fluorochemicals.name: Fluorochemicals
Fluorochemicals.descriptor_pill: HF, fluoropolymers, and refrigerant precursors derived fr...
Fluorochemicals.about: HF, fluoropolymers, and refrigerant precursors derived from fluorspar.
ai_summary: Family of fluorine-based compounds including refrigerants (R-134a, R-410A), fluoropolymers (PTFE, PVDF), and semiconductor etch gases (NF₃, SF₆).
Production is concentrated in China (~60% of global fluorochemical capacity), with Chemours, Honeywell, and Daikin as major Western producers.
Semiconductor fabs consume NF₃ for chamber cleaning and various fluorinated gases for plasma etching — volumes scale directly with wafer starts.
Datacenter cooling systems use fluorinated refrigerants — the HFC-to-HFO transition mandated by the Kigali Amendment is reshaping supply chains.
Immersion cooling for AI GPU racks increasingly uses engineered fluorinated fluids (3M Novec, Solvay Galden) whose supply is limited.
The fluorochemical chain is tightening from both ends — semiconductor demand scaling up while regulatory phase-outs constrain legacy products.

Uranium.name: Uranium
Uranium.descriptor_pill: Mined U3O8 yellowcake feeding LEU and HALEU enrichment cy...
Uranium.about: Mined U3O8 yellowcake feeding LEU and HALEU enrichment cycles.
ai_summary: Radioactive metal whose controlled fission generates heat for steam turbines — the only commercially proven zero-carbon baseload power source.
Global mine production is roughly 60,000 t/yr of U₃O₈, led by Kazakhstan (~45%), Canada, Namibia, and Australia.
Spot U₃O₈ prices rose from ~$50/lb in early 2023 to above $100/lb by early 2025, driven by utility restocking and AI datacenter power demand.
Microsoft, Google, and Amazon have all signed nuclear power agreements for datacenter supply since mid-2024.
Small modular reactors (SMRs) are being designed specifically for behind-the-meter datacenter power at 50–300 MW scale.
Every gigawatt of new nuclear capacity committed to AI datacenters locks in decades of uranium fuel demand — the restart cycle has begun and the supply chain isn't ready.

Zirconium.name: Zirconium
Zirconium.descriptor_pill: Nuclear-grade Zr metal for fuel-rod cladding; hafnium-fre...
Zirconium.about: Nuclear-grade Zr metal for fuel-rod cladding; hafnium-free purity is critical.
ai_summary: Corrosion-resistant metal used primarily as fuel-rod cladding in nuclear reactors — the structural tube that holds uranium fuel pellets inside the core.
Global production of zircon sand is roughly 1.2 million t/yr, with Australia and South Africa as leading producers.
Nuclear-grade zirconium requires complete separation from hafnium, a chemically near-identical element — only a handful of facilities worldwide perform this separation.
Westinghouse, Framatome, and TVEL are the dominant producers of nuclear-grade zirconium alloy cladding (Zircaloy).
The hafnium removed during zirconium purification is itself a high-value byproduct used as the gate dielectric in every advanced logic chip.
SMR deployment for AI datacenter power would increase zirconium cladding demand — and simultaneously loosen hafnium supply as a structural side effect.

Tellurium.name: Tellurium
Tellurium.descriptor_pill: Active layer in CdTe thin-film solar; byproduct of copper...
Tellurium.about: Active layer in CdTe thin-film solar; byproduct of copper refining.
ai_summary: Rare metalloid recovered primarily as a byproduct of copper refining — one of the scarcest elements used in any commercial energy technology.
Global production is roughly 500–600 t/yr, with China, Japan, and Canada as leading producers.
Almost entirely consumed by First Solar for cadmium telluride (CdTe) thin-film solar panels — the dominant non-silicon solar technology.
First Solar sources tellurium through long-term contracts with copper refiners and operates the only large-scale CdTe recycling program.
CdTe panels are increasingly deployed for onsite and grid-scale solar powering AI datacenters, particularly in the US Southwest.
Tellurium supply is gated three layers down the byproduct chain behind copper — it cannot scale independently of copper refining economics.

Cadmium.name: Cadmium
Cadmium.descriptor_pill: Paired with tellurium in CdTe solar; byproduct of zinc re...
Cadmium.about: Paired with tellurium in CdTe solar; byproduct of zinc refining.
ai_summary: Toxic metal recovered as a byproduct of zinc smelting, with global production around 23,000 t/yr.
Primarily consumed in nickel-cadmium batteries and cadmium telluride solar cells — the two applications that justify its continued production.
First Solar's CdTe thin-film technology pairs cadmium with tellurium in a semiconductor compound that converts sunlight to electricity.
Strict regulations on cadmium handling (EU RoHS, REACH) create compliance overhead but also barriers to entry for competitors.
Supply is adequate and tracks zinc smelting volumes — cadmium is occasionally an unwanted byproduct, depressing prices.
Cadmium's role in AI infrastructure is indirect but clear — it enables CdTe solar panels that increasingly power the datacenters driving AI compute demand.

Vanadium.name: Vanadium
Vanadium.descriptor_pill: Feeds vanadium pentoxide for SCR catalysts and redox-flow...
Vanadium.about: Feeds vanadium pentoxide for SCR catalysts and redox-flow battery electrolyte.
ai_summary: Transition metal used in high-strength steel alloys and as the electrolyte in vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs).
Global production is roughly 100,000 t/yr, led by China (~55%), Russia, and South Africa — primarily from vanadiferous titanomagnetite ores.
VRFBs offer near-unlimited cycle life and 4–8 hour discharge duration — characteristics well-suited to datacenter grid-scale storage.
Unlike lithium-ion, the vanadium electrolyte in a flow battery does not degrade — it can be reused indefinitely, reducing long-term storage cost.
Vanadium pentoxide prices are volatile, historically swinging $5–30/lb based on steel demand cycles and Chinese production policy.
If flow batteries gain share in long-duration datacenter storage, vanadium shifts from a steel additive to a strategic energy storage metal.

Silver.name: Silver
Silver.descriptor_pill: Front-side metallization paste in c-Si solar cells; ~10–1...
Silver.about: Front-side metallization paste in c-Si solar cells; ~10–15% of mined silver flows here.
ai_summary: Precious metal with the highest electrical and thermal conductivity of any element — used in conductive pastes, contacts, and solders.
Global mine production is roughly 26,000 t/yr, with Mexico, China, and Peru as leading producers.
Silver paste is the primary conductor printed onto solar cells — each GW of solar PV capacity consumes roughly 10–15 tonnes of silver.
Also used in brazing alloys, electrical contacts, and high-reliability solders throughout datacenter power and connectivity infrastructure.
Solar PV demand for silver has grown to ~15% of total fabrication demand, adding incremental pressure on a market historically driven by jewelry and investment.
As AI datacenters drive solar PV deployment for power, silver demand compounds on top of an already supply-constrained market.

Platinum Group Metals.name: Platinum Group Metals
Platinum Group Metals.descriptor_pill: Pt/Pd/Rh catalysts for fuel cells, SCR, and electrical co...
Platinum Group Metals.about: Pt/Pd/Rh catalysts for fuel cells, SCR, and electrical contacts; HDD platter underlayer.
ai_summary: Group of six metals (Pt, Pd, Rh, Ru, Ir, Os) with exceptional catalytic properties — South Africa produces ~70% of global platinum and rhodium.
Total PGM mine production is roughly 400 t/yr across all six elements, concentrated in South Africa's Bushveld Complex and Russia's Norilsk.
In AI infrastructure, PGMs are used in fuel cell catalysts (Pt for PEM fuel cells), hydrogen production (Ir for PEM electrolyzers), and hard disk platters (Ru).
Ruthenium is deposited as a magnetic recording layer on every HDD platter — AI training data storage still depends heavily on spinning disk.
South African mine supply has been declining due to shaft closures, labor disputes, and falling PGM basket prices.
PGMs sit at the intersection of hydrogen energy, data storage, and fuel cell power — three vectors that all scale with AI datacenter build-out.

Lithium.name: Lithium
Lithium.descriptor_pill: Brine or hard-rock lithium feeding battery-grade Li2CO3 f...
Lithium.about: Brine or hard-rock lithium feeding battery-grade Li2CO3 for all lithium cathode chemistries.
ai_summary: Lightest metal element, used as the charge carrier in lithium-ion batteries that provide backup power and grid-scale storage for AI datacenters.
Global production roughly 180,000 t LCE in 2024, led by Australia (spodumene hard rock) and Chile (brine evaporation).
Lithium carbonate prices collapsed from ~$80/kg in late 2022 to ~$10–15/kg by mid-2025, driven by Chinese oversupply and slower EV adoption.
LFP (lithium iron phosphate) chemistry dominates datacenter battery energy storage systems (BESS) due to lower cost, longer cycle life, and no cobalt or nickel.
Every GW-scale AI datacenter requires multi-hour battery backup — 4-hour BESS installations of 100+ MWh are becoming standard.
Lithium is temporarily in surplus, but the AI datacenter BESS buildout adds a new demand vector on top of the EV cycle — the question is timing, not direction.

Natural Graphite.name: Natural Graphite
Natural Graphite.descriptor_pill: Flake graphite mined and refined into anode powder; ~65% ...
Natural Graphite.about: Flake graphite mined and refined into anode powder; ~65% China mining.
stats: Syrah Resources, Nouveau Monde, South Star
ai_summary: Crystalline carbon mineral used as the anode material in virtually all lithium-ion batteries.
China produces ~65% of global natural graphite and controls ~90% of spherical graphite processing (the anode-ready form).
Added to US and EU critical mineral lists; China imposed export licensing on graphite in late 2023.
LFP batteries used in datacenter BESS installations use graphite anodes — each GWh of storage requires roughly 800–1,000 tonnes of anode-grade graphite.
Synthetic graphite from petroleum coke is the main alternative, but costs 2–3x more and carries its own petroleum feedstock dependency.
Graphite is the anode bottleneck that mirrors lithium on the cathode side — Chinese processing dominance is even more extreme.

Petroleum Coke.name: Petroleum Coke
Petroleum Coke.descriptor_pill: Refinery byproduct calcined into synthetic graphite anode...
Petroleum Coke.about: Refinery byproduct calcined into synthetic graphite anode and graphite electrodes.
ai_summary: Carbon-rich solid byproduct of oil refining, used as the feedstock for synthetic graphite anodes and as fuel in aluminum smelting.
Global production is roughly 140 million t/yr, with the US as the largest producer from Gulf Coast refineries.
Needle coke — the premium grade used for synthetic graphite electrodes and battery anodes — is a much smaller market of ~1–2 million t/yr.
Synthetic graphite anodes made from petroleum coke are the primary non-Chinese alternative to natural graphite in lithium-ion batteries.
Phillips 66, Graftech, and Showa Denko are major needle coke producers serving the electrode and battery markets.
Petroleum coke links the oil refining industry to the battery supply chain — a connection that becomes more relevant as datacenter BESS capacity scales.

Iron Phosphate.name: Iron Phosphate
Iron Phosphate.descriptor_pill: Cathode precursor pairing with lithium in LFP cells domin...
Iron Phosphate.about: Cathode precursor pairing with lithium in LFP cells dominating stationary storage.
ai_summary: Precursor chemical (FePO₄) reacted with lithium carbonate to produce lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode active material.
China produces ~95% of global iron phosphate and LFP cathode material — the dominant battery chemistry for stationary storage.
LFP has become the default chemistry for datacenter BESS because it offers superior cycle life, thermal stability, and lower cost per kWh than NMC.
CATL, BYD, and EVE Energy dominate LFP cell production, with Western capacity (Gotion, FREYR) still in early ramp.
Iron and phosphorus feedstocks are individually abundant, but the integrated conversion to battery-grade iron phosphate is a Chinese-dominated process.
Every MWh of LFP battery storage deployed at an AI datacenter traces back to Chinese iron phosphate chemistry — the chokepoint is processing, not raw materials.

Phosphoric Acid.name: Phosphoric Acid
Phosphoric Acid.descriptor_pill: Phosphate feedstock for LFP cathodes and broader battery ...
Phosphoric Acid.about: Phosphate feedstock for LFP cathodes and broader battery and fertilizer industry.
ai_summary: Produced from phosphate rock by sulfuric acid treatment — the primary industrial source of phosphorus for fertilizer and battery chemistry.
Global production exceeds 50 million t/yr, led by China, Morocco (OCP Group), and the US.
Battery-grade phosphoric acid feeds into the LFP cathode precursor chain — higher purity requirements than fertilizer-grade create a supply premium.
Morocco holds ~70% of global phosphate rock reserves, giving OCP Group structural leverage over long-term phosphorus supply.
Phosphoric acid is abundant at commodity grade but constrained at battery grade — the purity gap is where the supply chain tightens.
As datacenter BESS installations grow, battery-grade phosphoric acid becomes another example of a common chemical whose premium grade is scarce.

Boron.name: Boron
Boron.descriptor_pill: Boric oxide for NdFeB magnets and as a glass-strengthenin...
Boron.about: Boric oxide for NdFeB magnets and as a glass-strengthening additive in fiberglass.
stats: Rio Tinto (US Borax), Eti Maden, 5E Advanced Materials
ai_summary: Metalloid element sourced primarily from borate minerals — Turkey holds ~70% of global reserves and is the dominant producer.
Global boron production is roughly 5 million t/yr of B₂O₃ equivalent, with Eti Maden (Turkish state enterprise) and Rio Tinto Borates as the two major producers.
In semiconductor fabs, boron is the primary p-type dopant implanted into silicon wafers to create transistor channels.
Every advanced logic chip and DRAM die in AI hardware has boron atoms implanted at precise concentrations across billions of transistors.
Boron trifluoride (BF₃) and diborane (B₂H₆) are the standard dopant gases used in ion implantation — consumed at low volumes but irreplaceable.
Boron is a trace input consumed in microgram quantities per chip, but without it no transistor works — the definition of a structurally embedded dependency.

Arsenic.name: Arsenic
Arsenic.descriptor_pill: Group-V element pairing with gallium in GaAs wafer growth...
Arsenic.about: Group-V element pairing with gallium in GaAs wafer growth; copper-smelting byproduct.
ai_summary: Metalloid element used as the group-V dopant in gallium arsenide (GaAs) compound semiconductor wafers.
Global production of arsenic trioxide is roughly 35,000 t/yr, with China producing ~50% — primarily as a byproduct of copper and gold smelting.
High-purity arsenic (6N+) is required for GaAs wafers that form the substrates for laser diodes in optical transceivers.
Every high-speed transceiver laser connecting GPU racks in an AI datacenter is built on a GaAs substrate containing arsenic.
Arsenic is toxic and heavily regulated, which limits the number of facilities willing to handle high-purity material at commercial scale.
Arsenic is the element that makes GaAs lasers possible — small volumes, high purity requirements, and regulatory barriers create quiet but real supply concentration.

Phosphorus.name: Phosphorus
Phosphorus.descriptor_pill: Group-V element pairing with indium in InP wafer growth a...
Phosphorus.about: Group-V element pairing with indium in InP wafer growth and a precursor to phosphoric acid.
ai_summary: Nonmetal element used in semiconductor doping (n-type) and as the group-V component of indium phosphide (InP) wafers.
Phosphine (PH₃) gas is the standard n-type dopant in semiconductor ion implantation, complementing boron for p-type.
InP wafers — the substrate for every high-speed datacenter transceiver laser — contain phosphorus as half the crystal lattice.
Global phosphate rock production exceeds 220 million t/yr (for fertilizer), but semiconductor-grade phosphorus compounds are a tiny, specialized subset.
Morocco controls ~70% of phosphate rock reserves, though semiconductor-grade phosphine is produced by specialty gas companies worldwide.
Phosphorus sits at the intersection of two AI-infrastructure supply chains — doping every chip and forming the substrate of every transceiver laser.

Sulfuric Acid.name: Sulfuric Acid
Sulfuric Acid.descriptor_pill: Bulk industrial acid used to dissolve vanadium pentoxide ...
Sulfuric Acid.about: Bulk industrial acid used to dissolve vanadium pentoxide into redox-flow electrolyte.
ai_summary: Most-produced industrial chemical globally at over 260 million t/yr — the baseline reagent for mining, refining, and chemical processing.
Produced both from sulfur (a petroleum refining byproduct) and from smelter off-gases during copper, nickel, and zinc processing.
In AI infrastructure, sulfuric acid is consumed upstream in the refining of copper, nickel, cobalt, and lithium — every battery and cable traces back to it.
Also used in semiconductor wafer cleaning (piranha etch, SPM clean) at fabs producing AI chips.
Supply is generally adequate and geographically distributed, tracking copper smelting and petroleum refining activity.
Sulfuric acid is a structural enabler rather than a chokepoint — abundant but so deeply embedded in upstream chemistry that disruptions propagate widely.

Ethylene.name: Ethylene
Ethylene.descriptor_pill: Petrochemical feedstock for polyethylene and XLPE cable i...
Ethylene.about: Petrochemical feedstock for polyethylene and XLPE cable insulation.
ai_summary: Simplest olefin and the world's highest-volume organic chemical — the building block for polyethylene, PVC, and ethylene glycol.
Global production exceeds 200 million t/yr from steam crackers and ethane crackers, with the US, China, and Saudi Arabia as leading producers.
In AI infrastructure, ethylene derivatives appear as cable insulation (polyethylene), coolant additives (ethylene glycol), and construction plastics.
US Gulf Coast ethane crackers benefit from cheap shale gas, giving US-produced polyethylene a structural cost advantage.
Ethylene is a commodity with deep, liquid markets — supply constraints are rare and typically short-lived.
Ethylene is a background input to AI infrastructure — structurally present in hundreds of downstream products but not a supply chain chokepoint.

Ethylene Glycol.name: Ethylene Glycol
Ethylene Glycol.descriptor_pill: Antifreeze base for the 50/50 EGW blends used in direct-t...
Ethylene Glycol.about: Antifreeze base for the 50/50 EGW blends used in direct-to-chip cooling loops.
ai_summary: Organic chemical produced from ethylene — the primary coolant antifreeze and the feedstock for PET polyester resin.
Global production is roughly 40 million t/yr, with China and the Middle East as dominant producers.
In AI datacenters, ethylene glycol is the baseline coolant fluid in chilled water loops and precision air conditioning systems.
Propylene glycol is the food-safe alternative used in some datacenter cooling systems where environmental regulations require it.
Supply is adequate and commodity-priced, tracking ethylene markets and Chinese petrochemical capacity.
Ethylene glycol flows through the cooling loop of nearly every large datacenter — a commodity input consumed in volume but rarely constrained.

Epichlorohydrin.name: Epichlorohydrin
Epichlorohydrin.descriptor_pill: Reactive monomer with bisphenol A producing the epoxy res...
Epichlorohydrin.about: Reactive monomer with bisphenol A producing the epoxy resin in ABF and PCB laminates.
ai_summary: Chlorinated organic chemical used as the precursor for epoxy resins — the thermoset polymer binding fiberglass in PCB laminates.
Global production is roughly 3 million t/yr, with China, the US, and Europe as major producers.
Every FR-4 PCB laminate in every server board, switch, and networking card in an AI datacenter is made from epichlorohydrin-derived epoxy resin.
Bio-based epichlorohydrin from glycerol (a biodiesel byproduct) is gaining share, with Solvay as a leading producer.
Supply is generally adequate but concentrated in a few large chemical producers — Dow, Solvay, and Chinese state enterprises.
Epichlorohydrin is the chemical ancestor of every printed circuit board — an invisible but structurally embedded input to all electronic hardware.

Bisphenol A.name: Bisphenol A
Bisphenol A.descriptor_pill: Aromatic monomer paired with epichlorohydrin to make epox...
Bisphenol A.about: Aromatic monomer paired with epichlorohydrin to make epoxy resin.
ai_summary: Organic chemical produced from phenol and acetone — the monomer for polycarbonate plastic and a co-reactant in epoxy resins.
Global production is roughly 10 million t/yr, with China, the US, and South Korea as leading producers.
In AI infrastructure, BPA-derived polycarbonate is used in LED light covers, cable connectors, and equipment housings.
Also feeds into epoxy resin chemistry alongside epichlorohydrin — the two compounds together form the basis of all FR-4 PCB laminates.
Health concerns around BPA exposure have driven substitution in food-contact applications but have not affected industrial electronics uses.
BPA is a bulk petrochemical input to datacenter hardware — ubiquitous in plastics and laminates, commodity-priced, and not supply-constrained.

Soda Ash.name: Soda Ash
Soda Ash.descriptor_pill: Sodium carbonate flux lowering melting temperature in sol...
Soda Ash.about: Sodium carbonate flux lowering melting temperature in solar and architectural glass.
ai_summary: Sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) used in glass manufacturing, lithium carbonate production, and chemical processing.
Global production is roughly 60 million t/yr, with China, the US (Tata Chemicals/Ciner Wyoming trona deposits), and Turkey as leading producers.
In AI infrastructure, soda ash feeds into flat glass and solar glass production — the cover glass on every solar panel powering a datacenter.
Also used as a reagent in lithium carbonate production from brine, linking it to the LFP battery supply chain.
Natural soda ash (trona-based, from Wyoming) has a lower carbon footprint than synthetic soda ash (Solvay process), giving US producers an advantage.
Soda ash is a bulk chemical with modest AI-infrastructure linkage — primarily relevant through solar glass and lithium processing rather than direct datacenter use.

Tin.name: Tin
Tin.descriptor_pill: Lead-free SAC solder, EUV photoresist sensitizer, and zir...
Tin.about: Lead-free SAC solder, EUV photoresist sensitizer, and zircaloy alloying.
ai_summary: Low-melting-point metal used primarily in solder alloys that join electronic components to circuit boards.
Global mine production is roughly 300,000 t/yr, with China (~30%), Indonesia, Myanmar, and Peru as leading producers.
Every solder joint on every server board, GPU module, and networking switch in an AI datacenter contains tin-based alloy (typically SAC305: Sn-Ag-Cu).
Lead-free solder mandates (EU RoHS) shifted the industry to tin-rich alloys, increasing tin intensity per device.
Myanmar's Wa State mines, which supplied ~10% of global tin concentrate, faced production disruptions in 2023–2024.
Tin is consumed in billions of solder joints per datacenter — a ubiquitous input whose disruption would halt electronics assembly globally.

Gold.name: Gold
Gold.descriptor_pill: Bond wires, plated contacts, and ENIG PCB finish; small p...
Gold.about: Bond wires, plated contacts, and ENIG PCB finish; small per-unit volume but ubiquitous.
ai_summary: Precious metal prized for its corrosion resistance and electrical conductivity — used in wire bonding, edge connectors, and high-reliability contacts.
Global mine production is roughly 3,600 t/yr, with China, Australia, and Russia as leading producers.
Gold bond wire connects die to package in semiconductor chips — each advanced processor uses small but non-trivial quantities.
Copper bond wire has replaced gold in many applications, but gold remains standard for high-reliability and automotive-grade packages.
Gold's role in AI infrastructure is structurally present but small in volume — price sensitivity is low relative to chip value.
Gold is a commodity input in chip packaging rather than a supply chain chokepoint — ubiquitous, expensive per gram, but consumed in milligrams per device.

Copper.name: Copper
Copper.descriptor_pill: Most systemic input in the stack: chip interconnects, PCB...
Copper.about: Most systemic input in the stack: chip interconnects, PCB traces, busbars, transformer windings, cables, cold plates.
ai_summary: The metal with the highest electrical conductivity after silver — used in every wire, cable, busbar, transformer, and PCB trace in a datacenter.
Global mine production is roughly 22 million t/yr, led by Chile, Peru, DRC, and China.
A single large AI datacenter consumes an estimated 20,000–30,000 tonnes of copper across power distribution, cabling, and cooling systems.
Copper prices have traded above $4/lb through 2024–2025, with structural deficits forecast as electrification and AI demand compound.
Copper also serves as the primary interconnect metal in chip packaging (TSV copper, redistribution layers) and on PCB substrates.
Copper has 33 downstream connections in the AI infrastructure chain — more than any other raw material — making it the single most systemic input.

Aluminum.name: Aluminum
Aluminum.descriptor_pill: Heat sinks, rack frames, server chassis, busbars, PV fram...
Aluminum.about: Heat sinks, rack frames, server chassis, busbars, PV frames, cable conductor alternative.
ai_summary: Light, conductive metal produced by smelting alumina (refined from bauxite) using enormous quantities of electricity.
Global primary aluminum production is roughly 70 million t/yr, with China producing ~60% — the most energy-intensive major metal to produce.
In AI datacenters, aluminum is used in heat sinks, server chassis, cable trays, structural framing, and the conductors in some transformer designs.
Aluminum smelting consumes ~15 MWh per tonne — the industry is itself a major electricity consumer, competing with datacenters for power.
Bauxite is globally abundant, but smelting capacity is concentrated where cheap power exists — a structural parallel to datacenter siting economics.
Aluminum is a bulk structural and thermal input — abundant by weight but linked to the same power availability constraints that shape datacenter geography.

Metallurgical-Grade Quartz.name: Metallurgical-Grade Quartz
Metallurgical-Grade Quartz.descriptor_pill: Quartzite gravel feeding silicon-metal furnaces; less pur...
Metallurgical-Grade Quartz.about: Quartzite gravel feeding silicon-metal furnaces; less pure than HPQ but vastly larger volume.
ai_summary: High-purity quartzite ore (>99% SiO₂) that serves as the starting feedstock for producing metallurgical-grade silicon in submerged arc furnaces.
Major quartzite sources include Spruce Pine (North Carolina), Mauritania, Spain, and Norway — not all quartz deposits meet the purity threshold.
Spruce Pine is the world's dominant source of ultra-high-purity quartz, supplying the upstream feedstock for both semiconductor and solar silicon chains.
A January 2025 landslide near Spruce Pine temporarily disrupted access, highlighting the geographic concentration risk in quartz supply.
The quartz-to-silicon pipeline has multiple purification stages — metallurgical grade (98–99%), solar grade (6N), electronic grade (9–11N).
All silicon-based technology — every chip, every solar cell, every fiber optic strand — traces back to a quartzite mine, and the highest-purity mines are few.

Quartz Ore.name: Quartz Ore
Quartz Ore.descriptor_pill: Mined quartzite, primarily from Spruce Pine NC, refined i...
Quartz Ore.about: Mined quartzite, primarily from Spruce Pine NC, refined into high-purity quartz.
stats: Sibelco, The Quartz Corp, Norwegian Crystallites
ai_summary: Raw silica mineral (SiO₂) mined from quartzite, sandstone, and vein deposits — the most abundant mineral on Earth's surface.
Global production of industrial silica sand exceeds 300 million t/yr, with the US, China, and the Netherlands as major producers.
Most silica sand goes to glass, foundry, and construction uses — only a tiny fraction meets the purity requirements for metallurgical or semiconductor applications.
The purity gradient from commodity sand (~95% SiO₂) to semiconductor-grade quartz (>99.99%) spans five orders of magnitude in impurity tolerance.
Commodity-grade silica is not supply-constrained; the constraint is at the high-purity end where only a handful of deposits qualify.
Quartz ore is the geological starting point of the entire silicon chain — abundant in bulk but scarce at the purity levels that matter for chips and solar.

Iron Ore.name: Iron Ore
Iron Ore.descriptor_pill: Feedstock for structural steel, rebar, cold-formed framin...
Iron Ore.about: Feedstock for structural steel, rebar, cold-formed framing, GOES, and stainless.
ai_summary: Oxide mineral (Fe₂O₃/Fe₃O₄) smelted with coke in blast furnaces to produce pig iron, which is refined into steel.
Global production is roughly 2.5 billion t/yr, led by Australia (~35%), Brazil (~15%), and China (domestic low-grade).
Every AI datacenter building is a steel structure — the structural frames, reinforcing bar, and floor plates all trace back to iron ore.
Iron ore prices have traded in the $90–130/t range through 2024–2025, driven primarily by Chinese steel demand cycles.
Vale, BHP, Rio Tinto, and Fortescue control the seaborne iron ore market — the most concentrated bulk commodity trade in the world.
Iron ore is a bulk commodity input to datacenter construction — critical by volume but not a supply chain chokepoint.

Scrap Steel.name: Scrap Steel
